newsitem.title: UK: Trade groups make euro convention recommendations.
newsitem.headline: Trade groups make euro convention recommendations.

text.p: Financial market trade associations said on Thursday they have reached a consensus on how the euro should be traded in money market, bond and foreign exchange markets.

The group, supported by Cedel Bank and Euroclear called on the EMI, the European Commission and all EU member states to adopt the standards, which cover such thorny technical issues as day count, decimals and public holidays.

"Establishing harmonised euro market conventions will promote liquidity and transparency in the new markets, and prevent confusion and disputes for trading and settlement," the group said in a statement.

The financial groups backing the proposals are ACI - The Financial Market Association, the Banking Federation of the EU, Cedel Bank, European Federation of Financial Analyst Societies, European Mortgage Federation, International Paying Agents Association, International Primary Market Association, International Securities Market Association, International Swaps and Derivatives Association, Morgan Guaranty as Operator of Euroclear System.
The following proposals were made -
Conventions for the euro money markets
* The adoption of an actual/360 basis for the day count basis
* The adoption of a spot/two day standard for the settlement basis
* the adoption of a two day rate fixing convention for derivatives contracts
* TARGET operating days to form the basis for euro business days Conventions for the euro bond markets
* The adoption of an actual/actual basis for day count
* The adoption of decimals rather than fractions for bond quotation
* TARGET operating days to form the basis for euro business days
* No standardised practise recommended for coupon frequency
* Standard settlement dates for internationally traded cross-border transactions for the euro should remain on a T plus three business day cycle
Conventions for the foreign exchange markets
* The adoption of a spot convention for settlement timing
* The adoption of the rule of "certain for uncertain" for foreign exchange quotation
* The ECB (or its national central banks) should be responsible for the publication of a daily reference rate
